key_insight: OmniCapBench proposes a more precise way to evaluate audio-visual captioning by combining broad coverage with fine-grained localization. It helps reveal where multimodal models succeed or fail, instead of only giving a single overall score.
problem_solved: Current audio-visual caption benchmarks force a trade-off between global evaluation and local diagnosis: whole-caption metrics miss detail, local probes miss coverage, and LLM-based judges can be unstable. This paper addresses the need for a benchmark that can expose fine-grained capability limits in multimodal large language models.
method: Introduces OmniCapBench, a deep-structured evaluation framework for fine-grained audio-visual captioning.
Designs evaluation that balances whole-caption coverage with localized assessment of specific audio-visual details.
Uses a more structured benchmark setup to reduce reliance on unconstrained LLM judging and improve evaluation consistency.
impact: This benchmark gives researchers and practitioners a clearer diagnostic tool for understanding multimodal model behavior. It can guide better model development, targeted debugging, and more reliable comparison across systems.

paper_title: OmniCapBench: A Deep-Structured Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Captioning
paper_authors: Zhongyu Yang, Jiale Tao, Ruitao Chen, Zuhao Yang, Yingfang Yuan
